storeys_rule.perimeter: 11-14: plots on the city edge; photos (Lambot 1975, 1989) show 10-14 storey walls of towers; cap 13-14 storeys under the Kai Tak approach
storeys_rule.beside-yamen: 3-7: within 12 m of the Yamen compound; the 1989 aerial shows a low core around it
storeys_rule.interior-east: 9-13: east half; the 1989 aerial shows it almost uniformly tall
storeys_rule.interior-west: 6-11: west half; the 1989 aerial shows mixed mid-rise roofs
storeys_rule.+tiny: plots under 4 m2 capped at 2 storeys
storeys_rule.records-min: raised to the highest floor named in a clearance claim filed for this plot (GRS HKRS1255), plus one; a minimum, not a count
storeys_rule.photo-lambot1989: counted by eye on Ian Lambot's 1989 aerial (window rows, roof to base); see research/photo_match/storeys_counted.json
storeys_rule.fixed: yamen, temple, latrine, shrine: 1 storey; footbridge, steps: 0
storeys_rule.status: zone rule, checked by eye against the 1989 aerial (tall perimeter, low core round the Yamen, taller east); 4 buildings counted on the photo. A full photogrammetric fit is not done: see research/photo_match/README.md

meta.ground_rule: Spot heights in metres above Principal Datum: 1961 sheet 180-NW-1 inside and on the edge of the city (printed in feet, read by eye), 1984/1987 sheets on the surrounding roads, and the 2024 sheet only at the Yamen (original level) and well outside the old footprint (the park was regraded). Fitted plane plus a smooth (Gaussian, 28 m) blend of the residuals. Ground fell from about 17 m at the north edge to about 8 m at the south-east edge.

lanes.note: Widths are wall-line to wall-line on the 1:1000 sheet (line weight ~0.5 m), so expect +-0.3 m. Ground-level lanes only: upper floors often bridged over them.
